records.attributes: Adult body typically ~50-80 kg. Brain ~1.3-1.4 kg — the established figure — far above the mammalian allometric expectation for its body. Bipedal, sparsely haired, with precision hands, colour vision and a vocal tract built for articulate speech.

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — brain mass ~1.3-1.4 kg is a well-established figure (see Sources), with documented cognition for this species.
brain_profile.architecture: Massively expanded neocortex, especially association and prefrontal areas, over a standard primate plan; language areas (Broca's / Wernicke's) and a large hippocampal system support symbolic thought and autobiographical memory. Jerison expectation for a 70,000 g body is only ~211.5 g — the measured brain is roughly six times that.

cognition_model.summary: The symbolic generalist: language, cumulative culture, theory of mind and long-range planning, with cognition deeply social — most human thinking is done in groups, stories and institutions.

personality.justification: A restless, talkative idea-generaliser: it debates, invents, teaches and reframes everything as a story or a system, and gets bored by any settled routine.

skills: Language and cumulative culture (teaching, writing, technology)
Theory of mind and large-scale cooperation
records.behavior_model: Triggers: novelty or problem -> talk, tool use and recruitment of others; social exclusion -> intense distress and repair behaviour. Needs: food, sleep, belonging, status. Goals: survive, belong, build, be remembered. State changes: solitary reflection flips to collective action through communication.
records.relationships: Hominidae; closest living kin are the chimpanzee and bonobo (bridges claimed in their records). Domesticated the dog, horse, pig, cow and cat — several records in this batch are its partner species.
records.memory_model: Remembers: language, faces, debts, stories and skills across a lifetime, and across generations via culture. Forgets: unaided detail fast — hence writing. Misreads: sees agency and pattern everywhere, including where none exists.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Brain mass ~1.3-1.4 kg is the brief's established figure. Wikidata Q15978631 / ITIS TSN 180092 are the taxon anchors I am confident in; they are named in Sources. A single MBTI for a whole species is the coarsest read in this batch — flagged as such.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: language-capable agent with culture ledger (knowledge persists across individuals), theory-of-mind social modelling and tool-crafting behaviour trees.

records.relationships: Hominidae; sister species to the bonobo, and — with it — humanity's closest living kin (kinship bridge to the human record). Communities are hostile to neighbouring communities.
records.memory_model: Remembers: individuals, ranks, grudges and reconciliations for years; fruiting locations across a large range. Forgets: little of social consequence. Misreads: over-attributes intent in rivalry — a bias that fuels its politics.

records.relationships: Hominidae; sister species to the chimpanzee, separated by the Congo River; with it, humanity's closest living kin (kinship bridge to the human record).
records.memory_model: Remembers: individuals, bonds and slights, and who shares with whom. Forgets: grievances faster than its chimpanzee sister does — by design of its social system. Misreads: assumes affiliation is available even from strangers more readily than most apes.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: INFERRED deliberately: bonobo brain figures exist in scattered literature but none was in the brief's established list, so no figure is stated and the Jerison expectation is the stated basis. Bonobo 'peacefulness' is well documented but should not be caricatured — aggression exists, at lower rates.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: affiliative faction agent — tension stat that the group actively spends social actions to reduce; sharing economy in its utility weights.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A quiet, dutiful protector: the silverback's whole style is steady care — decide the route, keep the family fed and together, meet threats himself — with novelty a distant second to duty.

skills: Group leadership and conflict mediation (silverback role)
records.behavior_model: Triggers: rival male or threat -> silverback display, group bunches behind him; food patch found -> settled group feeding. Needs: abundant herbaceous forage, group cohesion. Goals: family safety and steady calories. State changes: slow days, sudden total mobilisation around the silverback.
records.relationships: Hominidae; the eastern gorilla, kin to the western gorilla and, more distantly, to chimpanzees, bonobos and humans in this batch. Groups are families; lone males seek groups to join or lead.
records.memory_model: Remembers: feeding ranges, individuals, and the group's history of encounters. Forgets: little socially relevant. Misreads: human observers were long misread as threats — habituation research showed the reverse can be learned.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: INFERRED: no brain figure stated (not in the brief's established list) — Jerison expectation is the stated basis, and body mass varies strongly by sex, so the expectation is a species-typical male-weighted figure. Taxonomy (species vs subspecies of G. beringei) follows the roster's naming.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: family-group agent with a leader-decision node; slow utility cadence, high cohesion, display-then-escalate threat ladder.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A lone, patient engineer-thinker: it lives inside a vast private map of the forest, experiments quietly, plans seasons ahead, and treats company as an occasional resource, not a need.

skills: Tool use and innovation (sticks, leaf tools; documented population traditions)
Long-range fruiting-map memory and seasonal planning
records.behavior_model: Triggers: mast fruiting -> travel to remembered trees, tolerance of others nearby; lean season -> wider ranging, bark and fallback foods. Needs: huge intact range, fruit calendar. Goals: energy economy above all — move slowly, waste nothing. State changes: near-motionless rest flips to purposeful long travel when the internal calendar says a tree is ripe.
records.relationships: Hominidae; the Asian great ape, kin to the gorillas, Pan and humans in this batch at family distance. Social structure is a loose network anchored on mother-offspring units.
records.memory_model: Remembers: individual trees and their fruiting rhythms across years — among the most demanding spatial-temporal memories documented in a non-human. Forgets: social detail of casual encounters fades; the map does not.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: INFERRED: no brain figure stated per the brief's list; basis is hominid kinship, the Jerison expectation above, and documented cognition (planning/tool studies, largely captive — wild cognition is harder to test, noted honestly).
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: solitary agent driven by a seasonal resource calendar; planning horizon measured in in-game months; nest-building as a nightly build action.

records.attributes: Adult body typically ~3,000-6,000 kg. Brain ~5 kg — the established figure, the largest of any land animal. Enormous ears, a trunk with tens of thousands of muscles, tusks, and a matriarchal society whose oldest females carry decades of ecological memory.

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — brain mass ~5 kg is a well-established figure (see Sources), with documented cognition for this species.
brain_profile.architecture: The largest land-animal brain (~5 kg, established), with a very large hippocampus and olfactory system and a heavy cerebellum serving the trunk. Jerison expectation for a 5,000,000 g body is ~3694 g — the measured brain exceeds even that. Much of the mass serves smell, memory and trunk control rather than cortex alone — size here is not a simple intelligence score.

cognition_model.summary: Memory made flesh: matriarchs remember drought refuges not visited for decades, herds recognise the voices and bones of their dead, and experiments document empathy, self-recognition in mirrors, and cooperation.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: The matriarch-teacher: it leads by remembered knowledge, keeps the whole extended family oriented and calm, and puts the group's welfare — especially the young and old — at the centre of every decision.

skills: Cooperative problem-solving; tool use (branches, fly-swatters, modified objects)
records.behavior_model: Triggers: distant rain or remembered drought -> matriarch-led travel; threat -> bunching defence with calves centred; death of a herd member -> prolonged investigation and return visits to bones. Needs: vast range, water, social continuity. Goals: herd survival across decades, not days.
records.relationships: Elephantidae; the herd is a family led by its oldest female, with bulls leaving at adolescence. Ecological engineer of its savanna — a keystone relationship to nearly everything around it.
records.memory_model: Remembers: routes, water, individuals (by voice and scent) and dangers across decades; the matriarch's memory is the herd's survival asset. Forgets: remarkably little that mattered. Misreads: old trauma sites can trigger alarm long after the threat passed — memory's cost.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Brain mass ~5 kg is the brief's established figure. Infrasound and recognition findings rest on long-term field research (Amboseli and similar). Neuron-count comparisons with humans exist but are method-sensitive, so none is stated as fact here.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: herd agent whose leader carries a persistent decades-deep map memory; infrasound as a long-range communication channel; grief behaviour state at deaths.

brain_profile.architecture: Large, highly convoluted neocortex organised around sound: echolocation and whistles are the primary world-channel, vision secondary. Measured brain (~1.5-1.7 kg) is roughly four times the Jerison expectation (~427.4 g) for a 200,000 g body. Unihemispheric sleep keeps one half of the brain awake to breathe and watch.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A playful, hyper-social improviser: it surfs, games, invents hunting tricks with its pod, and treats every encounter — fish, boat or stranger — as something to explore out loud.

skills: Signature whistles — individual 'names', remembered for decades
Cooperative and culturally transmitted hunting techniques
records.behavior_model: Triggers: fish school -> coordinated herding hunts; novel object -> inspection and play; separated calf -> signature-whistle calling. Needs: pod contact, fish, acoustic space. Goals: food, social standing, play — genuinely mixed. State changes: travel, forage, socialise and rest cycle through the day; one brain hemisphere sleeps at a time.
records.relationships: Delphinidae; kin to the orca in this batch. Society is fission-fusion with strong long-term bonds and, in males, multi-level alliances — among the most complex social networks known outside humans.
records.memory_model: Remembers: individual signature whistles for 20+ years (documented), hunting sites, companions and techniques learned from mother. Forgets: little socially. Misreads: boats and humans are investigated as social novelties — curiosity that can endanger it.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Brain mass ~1.5-1.7 kg is the brief's established figure. Whistle-recognition durations rest on long-term playback studies. Dolphin 'intelligence' rankings vs apes are method-contested; this record states documented behaviours only.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: sonar-first perception (acoustic world-model), signature-whistle identity ledger, pod alliance graph, play drive as a real utility term.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A commanding strategist hunting as a coordinated unit: every attack is a planned team operation, roles are assigned, traditions are enforced, and the matriarch's experience directs the whole pod.

skills: Culture-specific cooperative hunting (wave-washing, carousel herding, beaching)
records.behavior_model: Triggers: prey signature (by culture) -> rehearsed team tactic; unfamiliar prey type -> often ignored, however abundant. Needs: pod cohesion, traditional prey. Goals: pod feeding and calf teaching. State changes: travel in formation flips to synchronised attack choreography.
records.relationships: Delphinidae; the bottlenose dolphin's giant kin in this batch. Pods are matrilines; ecotypes (resident, transient, offshore) are cultures on their way to becoming separate species.
records.memory_model: Remembers: hunting grounds, techniques, pod dialect and individuals across a 50-90 year life. Forgets: little. Misreads: its own culture's menu as the only menu — specialisation is both its genius and its trap.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: INFERRED deliberately: the orca brain is famously large, but no figure was in the brief's established list, so none is stated and Jerison is the basis. Ecotype/dialect findings are well documented; claims of orca 'languages' beyond dialects would be overreach and are not made.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: pod-culture agent — technique and menu locked by culture ID, taught vertically; matriarch memory node; synchronised group tactics.

cognition_model.summary: A tiny, prolific commensal genius of adaptation: ultrasonic songs, scent-written territories, rapid learning and faster breeding. In the laboratory it became humanity's stand-in brain; in the wild it is a cautious, social, map-making survivor.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A small, wary opportunist-engineer: it maps its walls and warrens precisely, tests everything cautiously, sings ultrasonically for love, and survives by being quick, quiet and hard to predict.

skills: Rapid adaptation — the model organism of genetics and neuroscience
records.behavior_model: Triggers: new scent mark -> investigation and counter-marking; predator odour -> freezing and route change; food surplus -> hoarding and breeding surge. Needs: cover-dense micro-range, grain-rich food, water from food. Goals: stay unobserved, breed fast, cache. State changes: nocturnal activity pulses; population booms track food exactly.
records.relationships: Muridae; the brown rat's smaller kin in this batch. Wild social units are a dominant male, females and young; its second relationship — with human laboratories — has made it the most known mammal alive, noted as fact.
records.memory_model: Remembers: routes, refuges, food sites and scent geography. Forgets: fine detail faster than the rat — a shorter ledger for a shorter, faster life. Misreads: snap traps exploit its route fidelity — fidelity is both its map and its vulnerability.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Brain mass ~0.4 g is the brief's established figure. The 'most completely measured' claim reflects published whole-brain cell atlases for this species (Allen Institute and peers) — a provenance claim, checkable, and stated as such. Wild-vs-lab behaviour differences are real; the record describes the species, not only the lab strains.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: micro-map agent — wall-hugging route fidelity, scent-mark territory layer, ultrasonic channel invisible to most other agents' perception.

records.behavior_model: Triggers: sound of running water -> building at the leak point (documented, even against loudspeakers); intruder scent -> patrol and possible fight; autumn -> cache-building urgency. Needs: pond depth (predator safety, under-ice food access), aspen and willow supply. Goals: a pond that never drains and never freezes to the bottom. State changes: nocturnal work shifts; winter life under ice from the cache.
records.relationships: Castoridae; order-kin to the rat, mouse and mole-rat in this batch — Rodentia's engineer among commensals and colonists. The colony is a family: monogamous pair, kits and yearlings, dispersing at ~2 years.
records.memory_model: Remembers: pond works, food trees, cache position under ice, territory boundaries. Forgets: little within its watershed. Misreads: culverts and drains as dam sites — its engineering drive answers running water wherever it sings.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: INFERRED: no brain figure stated per the brief's list. The water-sound building trigger (including the loudspeaker experiments) is classic documented work. Beaver 'intelligence' claims beyond engineering behaviour are not made — the building IS the cognition claim.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.

records.memory_model: Remembers: puzzle solutions for years (classic studies retested after long intervals), food sites, dens and safe routes. Forgets: little that its hands learned. Misreads: human property boundaries as irrelevant — which, from inside its map, they are.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A devoted warren-keeper: it grazes close to home with its family, keeps the group's routines and hierarchies, raises kits communally, and puts the safety of the burrow above every adventure.

records.behavior_model: Triggers: predator silhouette -> freeze, then thump-and-bolt to the nearest entrance; stranger rabbit scent -> chase or investigation by rank; spring -> breeding surge and warren expansion. records.relationships: Leporidae; the batch's only lagomorph — kin at a respectful distance to the rodents it resembles but is not. Warren groups are extended families; domestic rabbits everywhere descend from this record's species.
records.memory_model: Remembers: warren layout, bolt routes, grazing grounds and group members. Forgets: little of safety geography. Misreads: myxomatosis and rabbit haemorrhagic disease arrived as threats no behaviour could model — history recorded in the population crashes.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: INFERRED: no brain figure stated per the brief's list. Warren social structure and alarm behaviour are well documented; rabbit cognition testing is limited, so claims stay at social/spatial level. Domestic-rabbit behaviour differs and is not folded in.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: warren-network agent — tunnel graph as home base, bolt-route escape planning, thump alarm propagation, grazing risk radius around entrances.

records.memory_model: Remembers: dens, routes, food trees and carrion sites. Forgets: social detail — it keeps almost none to forget. Misreads: roads and cars, again: slowness plus freeze instincts are a fatal modern combination.

records.attributes: Large, vividly scarlet-yellow-blue macaw, typical mass used here ~1,000 g; powerful beak cracks hard nuts and seeds; zygodactyl feet handle food to the beak. Strong pair bonds, noisy communal roosts, and regular visits to clay licks, where many parrots gather to eat clay (geophagy — commonly interpreted as mineral/toxin management). Long-lived, decades.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — Jerison expectation from typical body mass used here (1,000 g): E = 0.12 x 1000^0.67 ≈ 12.3 g. Basis stated: that expectation plus kin neuroanatomy and documented behaviour; no species-specific connectome exists. Bird caveat, stated rather than forced: pallial neuron density breaks the mammal line — as the raven pilot record explains (Olkowicz et al. 2016), birds pack far more pallial neurons per gram than mammals, so this mammal expectation is a reference figure, not a prediction of this bird's neuron number or ability.
brain_profile.architecture: Avian pallial plan in the parrot configuration: dense pallial neurons (parrots sit near the top of avian neuron-count findings), vocal-learning circuitry, and foot-beak manipulation loops. Cognition sketch from parrot kin; species-specific lab work is thin compared with the African grey.

cognition_model.summary: A loud, social, long-memoried canopy citizen: life is organised around a mate, a roost community, and a remembered calendar of fruiting trees and clay licks.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A flamboyant social enthusiast: it travels, calls, plays and displays in company, bonds for life, and turns every dawn roost departure into a public event.

skills: Hard nut/seed cracking with beak and foot handling
Long-range commuting between roosts and feeding sites
records.behavior_model: Triggers: fruiting tree located -> group recruitment by calling; dawn -> roost exodus. Needs: canopy food trees, clay licks, roost community, mate. Goals: calories, social place, pair maintenance. State changes: noisy group travel vs focused, quieter feeding.
records.relationships: Psittacidae, genus Ara with the other large macaws. Pair-centred within a larger roost/flock society; clay licks are multi-species parrot gatherings. Heavily affected by the pet trade and habitat loss — human pressure is a defining relationship.
records.memory_model: Long life plus stable roosts, licks and pair bonds imply durable spatial and social memory; stated as behaviour-based inference — macaw-specific memory experiments are not claimed.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: INFERRED: parrot neuron-density findings support a high-capacity pallium for the family, but scarlet-macaw-specific cognition studies are sparse; this record does not borrow the African grey's measured results as its own.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: roost-community social graph with pair bond at its centre, fruiting-calendar world memory, clay-lick gathering events.

records.attributes: Medium grey parrot with a scarlet tail, typical mass used here ~450 g. In the wild: social, roosting in groups, feeding on fruits, nuts and seeds. In research settings, the species of Pepperberg's Alex studies — referential label use and concept tasks that changed how avian cognition is assessed. Sensitive, long-lived (decades), and prone to stress behaviours in poor captive conditions.

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — cognition genuinely published: Irene Pepperberg's decades of work with the grey parrot Alex (label learning for objects, colours, shapes and materials; same/different concepts; a zero-like concept; numerical competence to 6) is peer-reviewed and replicated in its core methods, alongside parrot pallial neuron-count findings. Jerison reference for the typical mass used here (450 g): E = 0.12 x 450^0.67 ≈ 7.2 g — and, per the bird caveat in the raven pilot, pallial neuron density breaks the mammal line, so that figure under-predicts the neuron capacity the family is documented to carry.
brain_profile.architecture: Avian pallial plan, parrot configuration: high pallial neuron density, powerful vocal-learning circuitry coupled to associative systems that, in Pepperberg's training paradigm, supported referential labels and abstract same/different judgements.

cognition_model.summary: The measured mind of this batch: Alex labelled objects by colour, shape and material, answered same/different questions, and used a zero-like concept — referential, conceptual performance documented in peer-reviewed studies, not anecdote.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A concept-driven learner: Alex's documented work was categorising the world — what colour, what shape, what's same, what's different — the behaviour of a mind that sorts reality for its own sake, with a sensitive, easily stressed social side (hence the INFP runner-up).

skills: Vocal imitation and contextual call use
records.behavior_model: Triggers: novel object presented with social modelling -> label learning and questioning behaviour (Alex's documented 'what colour?' exchanges); social isolation or change -> stress signals. Needs: rich social interaction, forage complexity, flock/roost contact. Goals: social engagement and information. State changes: engaged learner vs withdrawn/stressed in barren conditions — a welfare-relevant state the record keeps explicit.
records.relationships: Psittacidae. Wild social structure is roost- and flock-based with pair bonds. Its defining human relationship is double: research partner (Pepperberg) and heavily traded pet species — it is endangered in the wild largely from trapping.
records.memory_model: Long-term label and concept retention over years was documented in the Alex work; wild memory is inferred from long life and stable social/spatial routines. What it misreads: captive greys are famously thrown by routine change — novelty in context, not object, is the stressor.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: MEASURED for the Pepperberg findings as published; caution kept: Alex was one intensively trained individual, later greys replicated core label/concept results with variation, and wild cognition is not the lab record. Extrapolating Alex to every grey would be an overclaim — this record grades the species MEASURED on the strength of a real research programme, with that caveat attached.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: label-learning module (objects gain names the NPC can request and use), concept-task drives, high social-need meter with visible stress states when unmet.

records.attributes: All-black crow, typical mass used here ~300 g, with a laterally placed bill and forward-facing vision suited to tool work. Manufactures tools in the wild: hooked twig tools and stepped tools cut from pandanus leaves, carried and reused. Family groups with prolonged juvenile learning; tool designs show regional variation consistent with cumulative cultural traditions (a debated but published interpretation).

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — tool behaviour genuinely published: wild manufacture of hooked stick tools and stepped pandanus tools, and laboratory problem-solving (including the Betty hook-bending study and later replications/qualifications), are peer-reviewed corvid-cognition literature. Jerison reference for the typical mass used here (300 g): E = 0.12 x 300^0.67 ≈ 5.5 g — with the bird caveat from the raven pilot: corvid pallial neuron density breaks the mammal line, so the small gram figure carries a primate-comparable neuron count.
brain_profile.architecture: Avian pallial plan, corvid configuration: the nidopallium caudolaterale (executive analogue) plus binocular visual control of a held tool — a sensorimotor specialisation visible even in bill shape and eye placement.

cognition_model.summary: The manufacturer's mind: it does not just use tools, it makes them to designs, keeps them, and improves on the problem in front of it — measured, published behaviour in both field and lab.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: An engineer by temperament: confronted with food in a tube, it does not wait for luck — it fabricates the instrument, tests it, and keeps the good ones.

skills: Hooked stick tool manufacture (documented in the wild)
Social learning of tool traditions (family groups)
records.behavior_model: Triggers: extractive-foraging problem (grub in a hole) -> tool selection or manufacture; discarded tool of good design -> retrieval and reuse. Needs: forest with pandanus and tool materials, grub prey, family learning time. Goals: extractive calories and tool-kit maintenance. State changes: foraging flips to focused workshop mode at a problem site.
records.relationships: Corvidae; close kin to the raven core of this Atlas (see bridge). Lives in family groups where juveniles have an extended apprenticeship — the social substrate of its tool culture.
records.memory_model: Remembers tool sites, good tool designs and productive trees; juveniles' long learning period implies durable procedural memory. Cache and observer effects documented in corvids generally are claimed here only at family level, labelled as kin inference.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: MEASURED for wild tool manufacture and core lab problem-solving. Qualifications kept: the famous Betty wire-bending result was later qualified (species predispositions and prior experience matter), and 'cumulative culture' remains an interpretation debated in the literature — both flagged rather than smoothed over.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: craftable-tool inventory as a first-class system (make, keep, lose, remake better), apprenticeship learning curves for juveniles, workshop state at problem sites.

records.attributes: Unmistakable black-and-white corvid with a long iridescent tail, typical mass used here ~210 g. Bold, noisy, opportunistic omnivore; builds domed stick nests; caches food; lives in pairs and loose winter groups with clear dominance interactions. Jerison reference for the typical mass used here (210 g): E = 0.12 x 210^0.67 ≈ 4.3 g — with the corvid pallial-density caveat from the raven pilot: the mammal line under-predicts corvid neuron counts.
brain_profile.architecture: Avian pallial plan, corvid configuration: executive nidopallium, cache hippocampus, and the social-perceptual systems engaged by the mirror study — body/self representation is the published anchor, stated narrowly.

cognition_model.summary: A bold social opportunist with a published mirror result to its name: curious, thieving, cache-minded, and constantly negotiating rank with its neighbours.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A showy improviser: it investigates everything shiny or new, argues its rank in public, steals strategically, and treats the neighbourhood as a debate it intends to win.

skills: Mirror-guided mark-touching (published study, debated — see Confidence)
Opportunistic omnivory incl. nest predation and scavenging
records.behavior_model: Triggers: novel/shiny object -> approach, inspect, possibly carry off; watcher at caching -> re-hide (corvid family pattern); mirror/mark paradigm -> mark-directed behaviour in the published study. Needs: open mosaic habitat, cache security, social place. Goals: calories, curiosities, rank. State changes: bold in groups, warier alone near threats.
records.relationships: Corvidae; kin to the raven core (see bridge) and to the New Caledonian crow of this batch. Pairs hold territories within a loose neighbourhood society of non-breeding groups.
records.memory_model: Cache memory and observer-sensitivity follow the corvid pattern documented in jays and ravens; magpie-specific claims kept to the mirror study and general caching behaviour. Long-term individual recognition of humans is reported for corvids and claimed here only at family level.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: MEASURED narrowly for Prior et al. 2008, with the honesty the study now requires: subsequent magpie mirror work has been mixed, and whether mirror mark-touching equals self-recognition is contested even for apes — the record flags the dispute rather than presenting self-awareness as settled. Folklore (counting rhymes, universal jewel-theft) is not behaviour and is not used.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: observer-aware caching inherited from the corvid template, shiny-object curiosity drive, neighbourhood rank graph; mirror interaction as a rare, flagged behaviour, not a self-awareness meter.

Basis stated: that expectation plus kin neuroanatomy and documented behaviour; no species-specific connectome exists. Bird caveat, stated rather than forced: pallial neuron density breaks the mammal line — as the raven pilot record explains (Olkowicz et al. 2016), birds pack far more pallial neurons per gram than mammals, so this mammal expectation is a reference figure, not a prediction of this bird's neuron number or ability.
brain_profile.architecture: Avian pallial plan with an outsized navigational system: hippocampal and sensory integration for a multi-cue compass, plus the visual categorisation capacity the lab literature documents for the species.

cognition_model.summary: A navigator that learns categories: it builds a map of a whole region, flies it home through shifting cues, and — in laboratories — has repeatedly shown finer visual learning than its street reputation suggests.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A loyal homebody: it bonds to one loft and one mate, flies extraordinary distances to return to them, keeps the flock's routines, and asks only for a ledge and seed.

skills: Multi-cue navigation (sun, landmarks, magnetic/infrasound cues — researched, partly unresolved)
records.behavior_model: Triggers: displaced from loft -> immediate homing programme; hawk shadow -> flock flush and wheeling escape. Needs: loft/roost ledge, grain and grit, mate and flock. Goals: home, food, mate. State changes: settled loft routine vs single-minded homing mode when displaced.
records.relationships: Columbidae. Wild rock doves, feral city populations and domestic breeds (racers, tumblers, fantails) are one species in three human relationships — cliff native, commensal, and bred athlete.
records.memory_model: Route and loft memory over years in racing birds is the practical foundation of pigeon racing; lab studies document long retention of visual categories. Misreads: a familiar feeding human is learned individually — keeper recognition is well attested anecdotally and consistent with its visual learning record.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: INFERRED by batch rule despite a genuinely large lab-cognition literature for pigeons (categorisation, numerosity, discrimination studies are published and real) — the grade is kept conservative because this harvest did not re-verify individual studies, and the navigation mechanism remains partly unresolved science. That conservatism is recorded, not hidden.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: true homing behaviour (displaced NPC navigates home by landmark memory), loft-anchored loyalty, flock-flush predator response.

Lives at sea for years, circumnavigating the Southern Ocean in dynamic-soaring flight that barely flaps; satellite-tracked individuals cover enormous distances. Breeds on subantarctic islands; pairs for life, but a pair breeds only every other year, and young birds spend their first years entirely at sea.

Basis stated: that expectation plus kin neuroanatomy and documented behaviour; no species-specific connectome exists. Bird caveat, stated rather than forced: pallial neuron density breaks the mammal line — as the raven pilot record explains (Olkowicz et al. 2016), birds pack far more pallial neurons per gram than mammals, so this mammal expectation is a reference figure, not a prediction of this bird's neuron number or ability.
brain_profile.architecture: Avian plan organised for oceanic endurance: navigational integration over a featureless ocean, olfaction (procellariiforms hunt by smell — krill and fish odours over vast water), and flight-economy control for dynamic soaring.

cognition_model.summary: A decades-long memory on the wind: it smells its food across an ocean, remembers a speck of island from years at sea, and returns to one mate on a two-year rhythm.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A faithful solitary pilgrim: years alone over empty ocean, one lifelong partner, one island home returned to across decades — a life of long patience and single deep attachments.

skills: Biennial breeding with extended chick-rearing (nearly a year)
records.behavior_model: Triggers: breeding year -> island return and elaborate pair courtship dances; non-breeding year -> continuous oceanic ranging. Needs: Southern Ocean winds, squid/fish/carrion at the surface, safe breeding islands. Goals: survive decades, raise a chick every other year. State changes: sea mode (years) vs colony mode (months) — the slowest state cycle in this batch.
records.relationships: Diomedeidae; pair-living at the colony, solitary at sea. Its gravest modern relationship is with longline fisheries, whose baited hooks drown albatrosses — a documented, ongoing conservation pressure.
records.memory_model: Colony and partner fidelity across decades, plus tracked returns after basin-wide journeys, support very durable spatial and social memory — recorded as inference from tracking and banding behaviour, not lab tests.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: INFERRED: movement ecology is superbly documented by satellite tracking; cognition is inferred from that record. Wingspan maxima are often overstated in popular sources — this record keeps to 'around 3 m and above for large males'.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: wind-gradient soaring movement model, biennial breeding clock, partner/colony memory that persists across simulated years at sea.

Apex predator and scavenger of its islands: hunts deer and pigs, dominates carcasses, climbs as a juvenile to escape cannibalistic adults, and can reproduce by parthenogenesis in the absence of males (documented in captivity).

Taxon caveat: the Jerison line is a mammal expectation; reptile brains scale differently, so the figure is a factory reference, not a measured brain mass for this species.
brain_profile.architecture: Reptilian plan on a monitor-lizard chassis — monitors are the active-foraging, high-endurance end of lizards: strong olfactory/chemosensory (tongue-Jacobson's organ) processing, spatial ranging over a home range, and dominance negotiation at carcasses. No cognition-measured programme exists for this species.

cognition_model.summary: An island apex built on scent and patience: it ranges widely, reads the island by tongue-flick, and lets size and persistence — not speed or pack tactics — settle every contest.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A lone physical operator: it patrols, samples the air, picks its moment, and relies on its own body and endurance — no pack, no display, no negotiation beyond dominance.

skills: Scent tracking of carrion and wounded prey
Juvenile tree-climbing to avoid adult cannibalism
records.behavior_model: Triggers: carrion scent -> directed travel; prey in range -> ambush rush; carcass contested -> size-based hierarchy, wrestling in males. Needs: home range with deer/pig prey and carrion, water, basking sites. Goals: large infrequent meals. State changes: slow ranging flips to explosive short rush; juveniles live arboreally, adults terrestrially — an ontogenetic state change.
records.relationships: Varanidae, the monitor family — kin to other large active-foraging lizards. Solitary except at carcasses and in mating contests; adults are the main predator of juveniles. Protected Indonesian endemic with a small, island-bound population.
records.memory_model: Home-range reuse and carcass/waterhole returns support spatial memory at the level expected of an active-foraging monitor — recorded as inference. No individual-recognition or learning studies are claimed.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: INFERRED explicitly, per the task instruction: the Komodo dragon is NOT a cognition-measured species — no lab cognition programme stands behind this profile; it rests on allometry, monitor-kin anatomy and field behaviour. Venom: gland anatomy is documented (Fry et al. 2009); how much venom vs trauma/sepsis decides real kills remains debated, and the old 'septic bite bacteria' story is now largely superseded — both sides flagged.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: scent-gradient tracking as primary perception, carcass-dominance contest system, juvenile arboreal phase as a distinct life-stage behaviour set.

records.memory_model: Site fidelity in very small ranges is the behavioural evidence for precise local spatial memory, recorded as inference. Pair recognition is implied by greeting behaviour; this record does not claim individual-recognition experiments for this species.

records.behavior_model: Triggers: client posing at station -> inspection and cleaning; audience of visitor clients present -> extra-honest service; client jolt (from a cheating bite) -> reconciliation behaviours (reported 'massage' appeasement). Needs: a station site, steady client traffic, parasite supply. Goals: parasite meals without eating the clients or the reputation. State changes: service mode vs cheating temptation, modulated by who is watching.
records.relationships: Labridae, the wrasses. Its relationships ARE its biology: resident clients, visitor clients, predatory clients, and partner cleaners at shared stations. The Bshary research programme made this species a model for cooperation and reputation in non-humans.
records.memory_model: Client-individual treatment differences and audience effects imply memory for clients and recent interactions — claimed as behavioural evidence from the published cooperation literature, which is genuinely about this species' system. Exact durations and mechanisms remain researched, stated modestly.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: INFERRED as a whole; the cooperation/audience findings are published and species-relevant. DISPUTED mirror claim, verbatim-honest: the cleaner wrasse mirror-mark study (Kohda et al. 2019, with a 2023 follow-up) reported that some cleaner wrasse scraped at a coloured mark after seeing it in a mirror, and the authors interpreted this as passing the mark test for mirror self-recognition. That interpretation is DISPUTED: critics argue the mark response can be explained without self-recognition (e.g. the mark resembling a parasite — a stimulus this species is specialised to remove — and mirror/social responses confounding the result), replication and interpretation remain contested, and self-recognition is NOT treated as established in this record. The dispute is recorded here in full because the claim is famous and the honest position is that it is unresolved.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: reputation system (service quality witnessed by bystanders changes future client traffic), client queue management, cheat-vs-serve temptation mechanic with jolt consequences.

records.attributes: Hermaphrodite has exactly 302 neurons (male 385) with ~7,000 chemical synapses plus gap junctions — every neuron named, positioned and wired in published connectomes. Transparent body, 959 somatic cells (hermaphrodite), ~3-week lifespan. Feeds on bacteria; senses chemicals, temperature, touch, oxygen and its own past feeding state.

brain_profile.architecture: No brain in the vertebrate sense: a nerve ring around the pharynx (the closest thing to a brain) plus ventral and dorsal nerve cords. Command interneurons (e.g. AVA, AVB, PVC) bias forward vs backward locomotion; sensory neurons feed layered interneuron circuits whose wiring is known synapse by synapse. Learning is synaptic plasticity inside a fully enumerated circuit — which is why this record can be scientist-grade.

records.attributes: Small spider with extraordinary principal eyes (acute, telephoto-like vision) on a brain that fills much of the cephalothorax. Hunts other spiders in their webs by plucking silk with a repertoire of vibratory signals, inventing new signals by trial and error when the first ones fail. Takes indirect detour routes that lose sight of prey for extended periods.

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — predatory tactics, detour behaviour and signal invention are documented in decades of controlled studies, largely by Jackson and Cross.
brain_profile.architecture: Salticid plan: large principal-eye visual system feeding a compact central brain. Vision dominates: Portia scans a scene slowly, plans a route, then executes it. Vibratory behaviour is generated and tested against the resident spider's responses — a feedback loop, not a fixed programme.

cognition_model.summary: The closest thing to a plotting predator among invertebrates: it studies a web, invents a lure signal, follows detours that hide the prey from view, and drops onto victims from silk lines. Patience and revision, not speed, are its weapons.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A solitary strategist that reconnoitres, builds a bespoke plan for each victim, and patiently revises the plan from feedback until the trap closes.

skills: Detour route planning with prey out of sight
Trial-and-error vibratory signal invention on webs
records.behavior_model: Triggers: web with resident spider -> scan, plan, signal-testing. Needs: spider prey, vantage points, time. Goals: eat dangerous prey without being eaten. State changes: if signals fail, repertoire expands; if the victim advances aggressively, Portia retreats and replans.
records.relationships: Family Salticidae; genus Portia species across Africa, Asia and Australia share the design. No social structure; courtship is cautious — the prey is also a predator.
records.memory_model: Remembers: which signal variants worked on a given web during an encounter, and detour endpoints while prey is unseen. Forgets: little is published on long-term retention — flagged as a gap. Misreads: an aggressive victim's advance can be misjudged, with fatal results — planning has limits.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Species-level detail is strongest for Portia africana, P. labiata and P. fimbriata as a group; some classic experiments used congeners, and this record attributes genus-level findings to P. africana only where the literature does. Long-term memory duration is genuinely under-studied.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: planner NPC — scan phase, plan object with detour path, signal-repertoire that adapts from target responses; working-memory slot for off-screen prey.

records.attributes: Large W-shaped pupils, skin that changes colour, pattern and texture in under a second via chromatophores, and a cuttlebone for fine buoyancy. Learns prey-handling, avoids crabs that have hurt it, and in experiments shows episodic-like what-where-when memory and future-oriented self-control (delaying a lesser prey for a preferred one).

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — learning, memory and delay-of-gratification results are published experimental findings, not anecdote.
brain_profile.architecture: Cephalopod plan: large central brain with prominent vertical lobe system (learning/memory), optic lobes, and a chromatophore motor system that renders the animal's assessment of the background directly on its skin. Embryonic learning occurs before hatching — chicks exposed to prey react to it after hatching.

cognition_model.summary: A visual intellect: it reads a background and prints it on its skin, remembers what it ate where and when in laboratory tests, and can wait for a better meal — self-control documented in a cephalopod.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.

skills: Delay of gratification for preferred prey
records.behavior_model: Triggers: background change -> pattern match; crab with raised claws (after a painful encounter) -> avoidance. Needs: shelter, shrimp/crab/fish prey, cover. Goals: feed while unseen. State changes: courtship adds bold signalling displays that override camouflage in males.
records.relationships: Family Sepiidae; kin to the pilot octopus core (same class, different body plan and social style). No parental care beyond egg-laying; adults are effectively solitary.
records.memory_model: Remembers: painful prey, profitable places, trained tasks for weeks. Forgets: within a 1-2 year lifespan, memory is a working tool, not an archive. Misreads: artificial backgrounds in experiments can fool the pattern system — camouflage is a best-fit render, not understanding.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Episodic-like memory and self-control findings come from specific laboratory paradigms (Jozet-Alves group); 'episodic-like' is the literature's own cautious term and is kept here. Wild cognition is less completely mapped than laboratory cognition.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: perception-to-skin renderer (background sample -> pattern state), what-where-when memory slots, delay-choice utility for prey selection.

brain_profile.architecture: Stomatopod plan: huge optic lobes serving the mid-band eye system, central brain integrating two independently scanning eyes. cognition_model.summary: A burrow fortress with superlative eyes: it watches the reef in spectral channels humans lack, remembers its burrow and rivals (stomatopods learn to recognise individuals in studied species), and answers intrusion with one of nature's fastest strikes.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A territorial sentinel that trusts its senses absolutely: observe from the burrow mouth, judge in an instant, and if the judgement is 'intruder', end the argument with a single explosive act.

skills: Cavitation club strike (prey smashing and defence)
Individual recognition (documented in stomatopods; inferred here)

records.relationships: Order Stomatopoda. Solitary; mating brief. Ecological neighbour to crabs and reef fish of this batch (Cancer pagurus is a distant crustacean kin).
records.memory_model: Remembers: burrow layout and (in studied stomatopods) individual rivals by scent/appearance across days. Forgets: little published for this species specifically. Misreads: its colour system favours fast spectral calls over fine shades — a design trade-off, not a defect.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Honest split: eye/strike facts are measured; species-specific cognition is thin — individual-recognition evidence comes from other stomatopods (e.g. Gonodactylus work) and is labelled inferred, not transferred silently.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: spectral-vision sensor with extra channels, burrow-anchored territoriality at maximum, strike as a high-cost/high-effect action gated by a threat assessment.

records.attributes: Workers cut leaf fragments many times their weight and carry them in processions to underground fungus gardens (Leucoagaricus), which they manure, prune and defend with antibiotic-producing bacteria on their bodies. Castes from tiny gardeners to huge soldiers. Colonies can run to millions of workers and excavate tonnes of soil.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — colony organisation, fungus agriculture and trail communication are documented; a colony-level 'cognition' profile is the Atlas's modelling frame, stated as such.
brain_profile.architecture: No single brain runs the colony: each worker carries a small hymenopteran brain (mushroom bodies for odour learning), and colony intelligence is stigmergic — trails, garden state and waste heaps are external memory. Trail pheromones recruit; leaf choice is collectively tested against fungal health.

regions.role: Odour learning — trail, fungus, leaf-quality cues

regions.role: Leaf selection/pruning decisions from fungal feedback

cognition_model.summary: Agriculture without a farmer: millions of small brains plus chemical writing produce leaf selection, garden hygiene, waste management and highway maintenance no individual understands. The pilot honeybee's colony logic, pushed to industrial scale.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: The colony as tireless operations manager: division of labour, supply lines, quality control of the fungus crop — everything organised, everything for the collective store.

skills: Pheromone trail recruitment and route maintenance
records.behavior_model: Triggers: scout finds suitable leaves -> trail laid -> mass recruitment; fungus rejects a leaf type (toxicity) -> that source is dropped. Needs: leaf flow, garden humidity/temperature, waste removal. Goals: fungal growth = colony growth. State changes: rain, predation or trail blockage reroutes the whole supply chain within hours.
records.relationships: Family Formicidae, tribe Attini. The colony record parallels the Macrotermes record in this batch — two unrelated lineages that both invented fungus agriculture; the Atlas keeps them as separate records, kinship by convergence noted here.
records.memory_model: Remembers: at colony level — profitable trees, toxic leaf types (via fungal feedback), trail geography. Individual workers learn odours for days. Forgets: abandoned trails evaporate chemically — forgetting is built into the medium. Misreads: a novel pesticide-laced leaf can be harvested before fungal feedback arrives.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Colony-as-entity is a modelling decision (as with the pilot bee). Leaf-rejection-by-fungus is documented behaviour; the internal decision mechanics are still researched. Population figures ('millions') vary by colony age and source — given as scale, not census.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: implement at colony level like the pilot bee — stigmergic memory (trails as decaying memory entries), caste agents, garden-health feedback as the colony's reward signal.

Workers farm Termitomyces fungus on chewed plant matter (fungus combs); soldiers defend with snapping/biting jaws and chemical sprays. A long-lived queen is the colony's reproductive core.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — mound engineering, fungus symbiosis and caste systems are documented; cognition is modelled at colony level, as with the pilot bee and Atta records.
brain_profile.architecture: Distributed system: individual termites are nearly blind workers with small brains; colony behaviour emerges from pheromone fields, mound state and garden feedback. The mound itself functions as an external organ — a lung and thermostat built by feedback, not blueprint (no termite holds the plan).

cognition_model.summary: A colony that builds its own climate: the mound breathes, the fungus digests, and millions of blind workers maintain both by local rules. Convergence with Atta (fungus farming) and the bee (colony memory) — three independent inventions of the superorganism.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: The colony as patient infrastructure-keeper: maintain the climate, tend the garden, repair the walls — duty performed identically for decades without novelty or display.

records.behavior_model: Triggers: mound breach -> emergency repair recruitment; garden CO2/temperature drift -> building behaviour adjusts airflow. Needs: dead plant matter, water, garden climate band. Goals: fungus growth and queen protection above all. State changes: seasonal alate flights found new colonies; drought deepens water-foraging.
records.relationships: Order Blattodea (termites are social cockroaches — kin, strikingly, to Periplaneta in this batch). Fungus-farming convergence with Atta cephalotes is ecological kinship, not taxonomy, and is recorded as such.
records.memory_model: Remembers: colony-level — mound structure itself is memory (where the gardens, nurseries and royal cell are). Individual learning is minimal and little studied. Forgets: pheromone information decays unless refreshed — the colony's working memory must be continually rewritten.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Mound ventilation mechanics were historically oversimplified (the classic 'air-conditioning' story); current work emphasises diurnal thermal driving and conduit geometry — record uses the cautious version. Colony sizes and mound heights are ranges, not fixed values.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: colony-level agent as with the bee/Atta — environment-as-memory (stigmergy), climate homeostasis as a drive, individual termites as near-mindless local-rule agents.

records.attributes: Orange-black warning colours over milkweed toxins sequestered from larval host plants. Four generations a year; the long-lived autumn 'supergeneration' migrates up to ~4,000 km and overwinters in dense fir-forest clusters. Antennae carry a light-entrained circadian clock feeding a sun-compass in the brain.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — the sun-compass/clock mechanism is documented; the full route-finding system (including any magnetic or inherited map components) remains partly unresolved, and the record says so.
brain_profile.architecture: Lepidopteran brain with mushroom bodies for learning (larvae and adults learn odours/colours), plus the navigation core: eye-derived sun position combined with antennal circadian time to compute a time-compensated heading. No individual learns the route — direction is inherited, destination reached by compass plus local cues still being mapped.

regions.name: Central-complex sun compass
regions.role: Time-compensated heading from sun position + antennal clock

regions.name: Mushroom bodies
regions.role: Odour/colour learning for nectar and host-plant choice

regions.name: Antennal circadian clock
regions.role: Light-entrained time sense feeding the compass

regions.name: Optic lobes
regions.role: Landmark and polarised-light input

cognition_model.summary: A compass with wings: it learns flowers like any butterfly, but its defining cognition is inherited navigation — a heading, a clock, and an overwintering forest it has never seen, reached across generations.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A gentle, single-minded traveller: no territory, no aggression, just colour, nectar and an unshakeable southward heading when the season turns.

records.behavior_model: Triggers: shortening days + cooling -> supergeneration physiology and southward heading; spring warming -> reproduction and northward relay. Needs: milkweed (larvae), nectar corridors, intact overwintering forest. Goals: complete the leg, feed, breed. State changes: reproductive diapause in migrants vs breeding in summer generations.
records.relationships: Family Nymphalidae. Migration is population-level: eastern (Mexican overwintering) vs western (Californian) populations are the same species — one record, two routes noted.
records.memory_model: Remembers: learned flower rewards for days; the route itself is not remembered but inherited — a critical distinction this record keeps. Forgets: individual flower learning decays. Misreads: light pollution and warming-shifted seasons can corrupt compass/clock cues (documented concerns, stated cautiously).
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Whether monarchs also use a magnetic map sense is unresolved in the literature — included here only as an open question. '4,000 km' is the upper documented scale for the eastern migration, not a typical individual total.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: compass module (sun + clock) as an inherited drive, not a learned map; generational relay — no single agent completes the full cycle.

brain_profile.architecture: Cerebral ganglion plus segmental cord: most processing is local and tactile/chemical. The worm's world is moisture, vibration, chemistry and darkness — cognition is gradient-following plus burrow-site memory rather than imagery.

cognition_model.summary: A burrow-centred gradient-follower: it tastes soil, fears light and vibration (predators), remembers its burrow mouth, and engineers the soil it lives in. Darwin devoted his last book to it for a reason.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A methodical soil-keeper: same burrow, same nightly rounds, leaves pulled in by the correct end — quiet, routine, indispensable work done in the dark.

skills: Leaf selection and burrow plugging (Darwin's observations)
Soil ingestion and casting — ecosystem engineering
records.behavior_model: Triggers: vibration/light -> rapid burrow retreat; rain -> safe surface wandering (and dispersal). Needs: moist soil, leaf litter, darkness. records.origin: Real species; tiny hydrozoan jellyfish (medusa ~4-5 mm) originating in the Mediterranean/Caribbean region and spread by shipping. 'Immortal' is the popular name; the biology is life-cycle reversion. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)

source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: When injured, sick or old, the medusa can collapse to a cyst-like stage and revert to a polyp — restarting its life cycle via transdifferentiation of its own cells. The cycle can in principle repeat, making the lineage potentially biologically immortal; individuals still die constantly to predation and disease. Nervous system is a cnidarian nerve net with a nerve ring — no brain.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — life-cycle reversion is documented in laboratory culture; any 'cognition' beyond nerve-net responses is inference, and there is very little to infer: this is a record about persistence, not intelligence.
brain_profile.architecture: Nerve net plus marginal nerve ring coordinating bell pulsation and tentacle responses. No centralisation, no learning studies of note. The remarkable system here is cellular, not neural: differentiated cells reprogram themselves back to a juvenile colony form.

regions.name: Nerve ring / nerve net
regions.role: Swimming pulsation, feeding responses, righting

regions.name: Transdifferentiation programme (cellular, non-neural)
regions.role: Medusa-to-polyp reversion under stress — identity rewritten at cell level

cognition_model.summary: Not a thinker — a restarter. Its fame is a cellular trick: when the medusa fails, it does not only die; it can fold back into its own polyp stage and begin again. The Atlas records the trick precisely, without the magic the nickname implies.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: If a type must be pinned to a nerve net, it is the quiet survivor: no plans, no territory — endure, drift, and when the form fails, become the earlier self and begin again. (Design metaphor — see Confidence.)

skills: Colonial polyp growth and medusa budding
records.behavior_model: Triggers: injury, starvation, temperature shock, senescence -> settlement, cyst formation, reversion. Needs: a substrate to settle on, plankton, suitable temperature/salinity. Goals: none beyond persistence and budding. State changes: the medusa/polyp alternation IS the state change — the whole record turns on it.
records.relationships: Class Hydrozoa. Kin in this batch: Hydra (fellow hydrozoan, famous for regeneration without reversion) and the jellyfish Chironex (scyphozoan/cubozoan branch, with real eyes and learning).
records.memory_model: Remembers: nothing neural is claimed. The 'memory' here is genomic/cellular — the polyp retains the medusa's genome, so the restart is genetically the same individual; whether any epigenetic trace of the medusa life persists is an open research question, not a claim.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: 'Immortal' must never be read literally: reversion is documented under laboratory conditions, repeatability in the wild and true indefinite cycling are not established facts. An MBTI read on a brainless hydrozoan is a design metaphor, labelled as such — the pilot principle stretched to its limit, honestly.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: nerve-net agent with a unique reversion mechanic — on lethal damage, a chance to revert to a polyp-stage entity with genome (stats) retained and neural state wiped. Persistence, not intelligence.

records.attributes: A filter-feeding barrel of spongin and spicules lined with choanocytes whose flagella drive water through the body. brain_profile.architecture: No nervous system — full stop. Coordination is by diffusing chemical signals and, in some sponge classes, propagating electrical impulses through syncytial tissue. records.attributes: A flatworm ~1-2 cm with a true brain (bilobed cerebral ganglion) and two ventral nerve cords, eyespots, and a body rebuilt by pluripotent stem cells (neoblasts). It can regenerate a complete animal from a small fragment — including a new brain. Classic and modern studies report trained responses surviving, in some paradigms, even decapitation and head regeneration.

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — with a live dispute carried openly: the memory-through-regeneration findings are published (notably Shomrat & Levin 2013, automated and controlled) but the field's history (McConnell's 1950s-60s cannibalism-transfer claims) includes results that failed replication. Both halves are in this record.
brain_profile.architecture: Planarian plan: bilobed brain integrating eyespot light, chemoreception and tactile input; ventral cords run the body. Learning paradigms show habituation, classical conditioning and maze performance. The radical datum is persistence: memories trained before decapitation were reported retained after a new brain regenerated — implying memory storage distributed or re-imprinted outside the original brain tissue.

records.origin: Real species; a plasmodial slime mould — a single giant multinucleate cell that creeps as a yellow network over rotting wood worldwide. No neurons, no brain, no cells-within-cells in its feeding stage. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)

source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: The plasmodium is one enormous cell with millions of nuclei, streaming cytoplasm through vein-like tubes whose thickness adapts to flow. It solves mazes by pruning to the shortest oat-to-oat path, builds networks comparable in efficiency to rail systems in famous experiments, habituates to harmless repellents (caffeine/quinine bridges, 2016), and anticipates periodic events after training in published work.

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — habituation, maze-solving and network optimisation are published experimental results; 'learning' here means documented behavioural change from experience in an aneural system, and the record uses exactly that definition.
brain_profile.architecture: No nervous system whatsoever. Cognition, if the word is used, is hydrodynamics plus chemistry: tube conductance adapts to flux (more flow, thicker tube), repellent and attractant gradients bias growth, and cytoplasmic oscillation patterns encode timing. Memory lives in tube morphology and in deposited slime trails — the network outside the 'mind' remembers where the mind has been (it avoids its own slime: externalised spatial memory).

regions.name: Tube-network adaptation (flow feedback)
regions.role: Route optimisation — the maze-solving mechanism

regions.name: Chemosensory growth front
regions.role: Attractant approach / repellent avoidance and habituation

regions.role: Periodic-event anticipation in published experiments

cognition_model.summary: The Atlas's flagship aneural learner: it habituates, anticipates, optimises networks and remembers spatially — all as one cell with zero neurons. Every claim here is a published experiment; the wonder needs no exaggeration.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: Pinned as an explicit design metaphor (see Confidence): a tireless network experimenter — extend a probe, measure the flow, prune what fails, keep the shortest path. It is the purest 'try and revise' system in the Atlas.

Externalised spatial memory via slime trails
records.behavior_model: Triggers: oat (food) gradient -> growth toward; repellent -> avoidance that habituates with repeated harmless exposure. Needs: moisture, shade, bacterial/yeast food, surfaces to creep on. Goals: maximise nutrient intake per network cost. State changes: starvation triggers sporulation — the network converts to fruiting bodies and ends as a network.
records.relationships: Kingdom-level placement: Amoebozoa, class Myxogastria — not an animal, not a fungus (historically mistaken for one). Atlas kin: Dictyostelium in this batch is the other slime mould, with the opposite social design (many cells aggregating vs one giant cell).
records.memory_model: Remembers: routes (in tube thickness), explored ground (in slime), repellent harmlessness (habituation lasting days), periodic intervals (hours, in the anticipation studies). Forgets: habits decay when conditions change; dried sclerotia pause the ledger for months. Misreads: a habituated repellent that becomes genuinely harmful would be crossed — habituation is a bet, not knowledge.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: An MBTI read on a slime mould is a design metaphor, labelled as such — there is no personality here, only dynamics worth borrowing. 'Anticipation' and 'learning' use the behavioural definitions of the source papers; no claim of subjective experience is made or implied.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: no brain object — a flow-network simulator: tube conductances as weights, growth/pruning as learning. The proof-of-concept that BrainKit cognition need not be neural.

records.origin: Real species; carnivorous plant native only to a small wetland region around Wilmington, North Carolina. No neurons, no muscles — a counting plant. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)

source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: Each trap is a modified leaf: two lobes with trigger hairs, which snap shut in ~100 ms when triggered. The counting mechanism is published: one touch raises a signal but does not close the trap; a second touch within roughly 20-30 seconds crosses the threshold, fires action potentials, and closes it. Further struggles by prey trigger digestive-enzyme production scaled to touch counts — the plant counts to two to close, and higher to invest in digestion.

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — the two-touch counting window and the touch-scaled enzyme response are published experimental results (Böhm et al. 2016 and successors).
brain_profile.architecture: No nervous system: electrical action potentials (plant-style, calcium-based) propagate through the leaf, and a short-lived chemical/electrical trace of the first touch is the 'memory' the second touch reads. Snap closure is turgor mechanics — stored elastic energy released by cell changes. A memory of seconds, implemented in ions.

regions.name: Trigger-hair mechanosensors
regions.role: Touch detection on the trap surface

regions.name: Action-potential counter
regions.role: Two touches within ~20-30 s = closure; more touches = digestion investment

regions.name: Trap motor leaf (turgor system)
regions.role: Snap closure and sealing

regions.name: Gland secretion system
regions.role: Enzyme release scaled to prey struggle counts

cognition_model.summary: It counts to two. A first touch is noted and held for seconds; a second touch in time means prey, not rain — and the trap fires. The smallest, cleanest decision circuit in the plant kingdom, fully published.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: Pinned as a design metaphor (see Confidence): a patient, rule-bound ambusher — nothing wasted, nothing chased; the rule is the rule, and it is executed in a tenth of a second.

skills: Two-touch counting with a ~20-30 s memory window
Lure nectar secretion on trap surfaces
records.behavior_model: Triggers: first trigger-hair touch -> primed state (~20-30 s); second touch -> snap; prey struggling -> escalating enzyme secretion. Needs: intense sun, wet nutrient-poor soil, live prey of the right size. Goals: nitrogen. State changes: digestion takes days, trap reopens with the husk remaining; false alarms cost a day of trap time — hence the counting.
records.relationships: Family Droseraceae (sundew kin). In the Atlas it pairs with Mimosa pudica as the plant pair: one counts touches to eat, the other folds to defend — both aneural, both electrical.
records.memory_model: Remembers: one touch, for about twenty seconds — the most precisely bounded memory in the Atlas. Forgets: everything else; each trap lives weeks and fires only a few times before senescing. Misreads: raindrops and debris are filtered by the two-touch rule, imperfectly — a dropped leaf-litter tap at the wrong moment can waste a trap cycle.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: An MBTI read on a plant is a design metaphor, labelled as such. The ~20 s window varies with conditions and study (values around 20-30 s appear); recorded as approximate. No cognition beyond the documented mechanism is claimed.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: a two-state counter with a decay timer as the entire 'brain' — the Atlas's minimal honest decision circuit, and a calibration point beside E. coli.

records.attributes: Leaflets fold and leaf stalks droop in seconds after touch, shaking or heat — driven by pulvini (joint-like motor organs) losing turgor as ions and water shift, signalled by propagating electrical potentials. The response is a defence display (smaller, thornier-seeming target) and startle device. Gagliano's 2014 study reported habituation learning (dropping-assay) retained for weeks — a claim debated in plant-science commentary.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — movement physiology is documented; the stronger 'learning/memory' claim rests on one research group's studies with published criticism and mixed reception, so the Atlas grades cautiously.
brain_profile.architecture: Electrical signalling without neurons: action potentials trigger pulvinus cells to dump potassium and water, collapsing turgor — the leaf folds like a row of hinges losing pressure. Recovery takes minutes as pumps restore the gradient. Any 'memory' would live in signalling thresholds or gene-expression states, mechanisms still argued over.

records.attributes: Trunk bark up to ~60-90 cm thick, fibrous and tannin-rich — fire and insect resistance without a single defensive behaviour. Cones can stay closed for years until fire heat opens them (serotiny) and seeds fall onto ash-cleared soil. Height growth is a hydraulic achievement: water lifted 80+ metres by transpiration tension. Root systems are broad and shallow, often interlocked with neighbours.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — there is no cognition; the record is the Atlas's timescale extreme: adaptive 'decisions' (fire-timed reproduction, hydraulic architecture) executed by development and chemistry across millennia.
brain_profile.architecture: Coordination without a centre: auxin and other hormones pattern growth; stomata trade water for carbon leaf by leaf; the vascular system integrates drought signals (including root-to-shoot chemical messengers) across a body taller than a 25-storey building. Response times run from minutes (stomata) to decades (crown architecture).

records.attributes: The visible mushrooms are fruiting bodies; the organism is a mycelial network in soil and wood, foraging with black shoestring-like rhizomorphs, infecting tree roots (white rot / root disease) and digesting dead wood. The Malheur genet was identified by genetic testing across the site — one individual, spreading vegetatively for millennia. Mycelia transport nutrients along the network toward growth fronts and fruiting.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — network foraging and nutrient translocation are documented mycology; any cognition language is metaphor and is labelled. The record's substance is scale and persistence.
brain_profile.architecture: No nervous system: coordination is chemical and hydraulic across a network with no centre and no map. Rhizomorph tips sense food gradients; translocation streams resources from rich patches (dead wood) to expansion fronts. The network's 'decisions' are growth economics written in hyphae — closer in spirit to Physarum's flow logic than to any brain, by convergence.

Goals: none attributable — growth and digestion are constitutive. State changes: drought pauses expansion; host death converts parasitism to saprobic digestion seamlessly.
records.relationships: Kingdom Fungi — closer kin to animals than to plants, a fact the Atlas map should show. Named kin in-batch: Saccharomyces (a fellow fungus reduced to one cell — the phylum's two size extremes in one batch). The Malheur individual is the famous genet; the species is widespread.
records.memory_model: Remembers: nothing neurally. The network's extent IS its history — which trees it has eaten is written in its map of cords. Source-sink translocation gives a functional 'preference' for proven food patches, recorded as economics, not memory.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Size/age figures: ~9 km2 (often quoted ~965 ha) and age estimates from ~2,000 to ~8,000+ years vary by method and source — recorded as estimates with wide bars. 'Largest organism' depends on the metric (area/mass); the sequoia record holds the single-tree volume title — no conflict once metrics are named. MBTI = design metaphor, labelled.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: resource-flow network agent (like Physarum but slower and persistent) — translocation weights, foraging fronts, no neural object.

records.origin: Real species; the single-celled fungus behind bread, beer and wine, and a premier model organism of cell biology. One cell, no neurons — signalling is the whole story. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)
