source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: A ~5-10 um cell that buds asexually, or — when starved — sporulates; two mating types (a and alpha) sense each other's pheromones and grow toward them (the 'shmoo'), fusing to form diploids. Its pheromone MAP-kinase cascade is the textbook eukaryotic signalling pathway, homologous in design to pathways in animal neurons. Glucose sensing flips the cell between fermentation and respiration (the Crabtree effect).

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — the signalling pathways are MEASURED cell biology; calling this a cognition record is the Atlas's deliberate minimal framing, and the record says so.
brain_profile.architecture: No neurons, no synapses: receptors -> G-proteins -> kinase cascades -> gene expression and cytoskeletal polarisation. The cell computes gradients (of pheromone, of glucose) and commits — mating, budding, sporulation are decisions in the biochemical sense the Atlas uses for its floor-level records.

regions.role: Ferment-vs-respire and grow-vs-sporulate decisions

cognition_model.summary: A single cell that sniffs for mates, tastes sugar, and chooses between feasting, mating and armoured sleep. The Atlas's minimal honest record for a eukaryote: everything here is a published pathway, nothing is a mind.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: Pinned as a design metaphor (see Confidence): a small sensualist — follow the sweetness, lean toward the mate's scent, and when times turn hard, seal up and wait.

records.behavior_model: Triggers: opposite-mating-type pheromone -> arrest and polarised growth toward source; glucose abundance -> fermentation even with oxygen present; starvation (diploid) -> sporulation. Needs: sugars, nitrogen, trace minerals. Goals: none attributable — growth/mating/sporulation as pathway outcomes. State changes: spore dormancy can outlast years of bad conditions.
records.relationships: Kingdom Fungi, phylum Ascomycota — the single-celled counterweight to Armillaria in this batch (same kingdom, ~15 orders of magnitude apart in size). Model-organism kin to every eukaryote record via shared pathway design.
records.memory_model: Remembers: nothing beyond pathway states and epigenetic marks (prion-like states such as [PSI+] are documented heritable protein conformations — a molecular inheritance, noted without cognition claims). Forgets: gradient information instantly when the signal stops.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: No learning or memory in the behavioural sense is claimed. Prion-based inheritance is real yeast biology but is included as chemistry, not cognition. An MBTI read on a yeast cell is a design metaphor at maximum stretch, labelled as such.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: biochemical decision-switch agent — three attractor states (grow / mate / sporulate) driven by nutrient and pheromone inputs. A floor-level calibration beside E. coli.

records.origin: Real species; gut bacterium of warm-blooded animals and the most studied organism on Earth. Its chemotaxis system holds a 'memory' of a few seconds — the smallest honest cognition record in the Atlas. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)
Established chemotaxis literature (Berg, Adler onward — Che protein methylation adaptation system)
source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: A rod ~2 um long swimming with rotating flagella in runs and tumbles. Chemotaxis: receptors detect attractants/repellents; a two-component signalling cascade (Che proteins) sets tumble frequency, and receptor methylation slowly resets sensitivity — comparing 'now' against 'a few seconds ago' is the bacterium's entire memory, and it is enough to climb gradients. Most strains are harmless gut commensals; some lineages cause serious disease (recorded for completeness, not emphasis).

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED as cognition, MEASURED as biochemistry — the methylation-based adaptation circuit is among the most completely characterised signalling systems in biology; the Atlas frames it as seconds-scale memory in the strict behavioural sense (present behaviour depends on seconds-past conditions).
brain_profile.architecture: No neurons, no synapses: a protein circuit with a built-in short-term store. Methylation level integrates recent receptor occupancy; the difference between current signal and methylation baseline steers the flagellar motor. It is a differentiator — a machine for sensing change, implemented in covalent chemistry.

regions.name: Chemoreceptor arrays (MCPs)
regions.role: Attractant/repellent detection at the cell pole

regions.name: Che signalling cascade + methylation store
regions.role: Seconds-scale adaptation memory — the whole 'brain'

regions.name: Flagellar motor switching
regions.role: Run vs tumble — the single behavioural output

cognition_model.summary: It remembers four seconds. That is the record, and it is magnificent: a protein circuit compares the present with the immediate past and steers by the difference — memory, decision and action in a cell with no neurons, fully characterised by science.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: Pinned as a design metaphor (see Confidence): a pure reactor — sample, compare, move; no plans, no attachments, just exquisite responsiveness to change.

skills: Chemotaxis up attractant / down repellent gradients
records.behavior_model: Triggers: attractant rise -> longer runs; repellent rise -> tumbling. Needs: nutrients, suitable temperature/osmolarity, a surface or gut to inhabit. Goals: none attributable — gradient-climbing is circuit behaviour. State changes: starvation triggers stress programmes and, in populations, biofilm lifestyles.
records.relationships: Domain Bacteria — the deepest branch in this batch; every other record is a eukaryote. Its chemotaxis design (receptor -> adaptation store -> motor) is the Atlas's template for 'cognition before neurons' discussions, paired with yeast as the prokaryote/eukaryote minimal pair.
records.memory_model: Remembers: the last few seconds of chemical history, as methylation. Forgets: everything older — by design; a longer memory would make it climb stale gradients. Misreads: a uniformly rich environment saturates adaptation and the cell tumbles blind — the circuit senses change, not abundance.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Memory duration varies with conditions (roughly 1-10 s in the literature); 'a few seconds' is the honest summary. No learning beyond adaptation is claimed; the LTEE (long-term evolution experiment) is population genetics, not individual cognition, and is listed as such. MBTI = design metaphor at maximum stretch, labelled.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: the absolute floor agent — one integrator (methylation), one comparator, one binary motor. If a BrainKit creature is simpler than this, it is not sensing change at all.

records.attributes: Body of fused segments, each with its own ganglion on a ventral cord under a small cerebral ganglion — identified neurons (touch, pressure, nociceptive cells) mapped cell by cell. Feeds on vertebrate blood, swelling many times its weight, then fasting for months. Swimming and crawling are central-pattern-generator behaviours; it habituates and sensitises to touch in classic learning experiments.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — identified-neuron neurobiology and simple learning are documented for leeches (much work on Hirudo and close kin); a full cognitive profile is an Atlas construction from those anchors.
brain_profile.architecture: Segmental design: 21 midbody ganglia, each a semi-autonomous module with the same identified sensory/motor neurons, coordinated by intersegmental interneurons. Local bending, shortening and swimming emerge from the chain. Learning (habituation, sensitisation, associative effects) modifies synapses in these known circuits.

cognition_model.summary: A chain of small brains that learns: it finds hosts by ripple and warmth, feeds enormously, and its habituation to harmless touch — in circuits whose neurons have names — helped found the cellular study of learning alongside Aplysia.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A patient tactile specialist: wait in the shallows, read the ripples, attach without being noticed, and hold on. Sensation-led, unhurried, solitary.

records.behavior_model: Triggers: water disturbance + warmth -> host-seeking swim; repeated harmless touch -> habituated non-response; noxious touch -> sensitised withdrawal. Needs: a blood meal a few times a year, clean freshwater, hosts. Goals: feed rarely and hugely; breed after feeding. State changes: fed vs hungry leeches are behaviourally different animals — hunger drives boldness.
records.relationships: Phylum Annelida — kin to the earthworm in this batch (same phylum: one drinks blood, one eats soil; both run on segmental cords). Neurobiology kin to Aplysia: the two classic identified-neuron learning preparations.
records.memory_model: Remembers: habituated stimuli for hours-days in experiments; satiety state for months (a physiological memory). Forgets: habituations decay without reinforcement. Misreads: warm moving objects that are not hosts get investigated — host cues are heuristics.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Much classic leech learning work used Hirudo medicinalis sensu lato; taxonomy of medicinal leeches was revised (H. verbana does much commercial duty) — noted so the record does not overclaim species purity of the older literature.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: modular ganglion-chain brain — reusable segment modules, habituation/sensitisation synapse parameters, satiety state as a master drive gate.

records.origin: Real species; Pacific coast sea slug and THE classical cellular model of memory — Eric Kandel's Nobel-winning work was built on its gill-withdrawal reflex. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)
Kandel tradition — Cellular Basis of Behavior (1976) onward; siphon/gill-withdrawal learning literature (habituation, sensitisation, classical conditioning; CREB molecular switch)
source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: A soft sea slug to ~5 kg with ~20,000 large, identifiable neurons in nine ganglia — neurons so big and consistent that the same cell (e.g. sensory neuron LE, motor neuron L7) can be found in every animal. The siphon/gill-withdrawal circuit is wired cell-to-cell in the literature. Repeated touch habituates the reflex; a tail shock sensitises it for days-weeks via serotonin, cAMP and CREB-mediated gene expression — short-term memory as synaptic facilitation, long-term memory as new synaptic growth.

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — arguably the most completely explained learning in neuroscience: behaviour, circuit, synapse and molecule all published, replicated and Nobel-recognised (Kandel, 2000).
brain_profile.architecture: Centralised ganglia ring (cerebral, pleural, pedal, abdominal) around the oesophagus. The abdominal ganglion runs the defensive withdrawal circuit: siphon sensory neurons synapse directly and via interneurons onto gill motor neurons. Serotonergic modulation from tail input strengthens those synapses (sensitisation); repeated low-rate activation weakens them (habituation); pairing yields classical conditioning. CREB transcription converts repeated training into lasting structural change — the record can name the molecule because the science did.

regions.name: Abdominal ganglion withdrawal circuit (LE sensory -> L7 motor)
regions.role: The measured learning circuit — habituation, sensitisation, conditioning

regions.name: Cerebral ganglion
regions.role: Head sensory integration, feeding initiation

regions.name: Pleural/pedal ganglia
regions.role: Tail-shock modulatory input and locomotion

regions.name: Ink/opaline defence system
regions.role: Chemical screen release under strong threat

cognition_model.summary: The animal that taught science how memory works at a synapse. Everything the Atlas claims about learning anywhere else is, historically, downstream of experiments on this slug's reflexes.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A gentle, defensive grazer whose whole documented inner life is learning what is safe: touch it kindly and it relaxes its guard; hurt it once and it remembers for weeks. Caution earned by experience, exactly as measured.

skills: Sensitisation after noxious shock — days to weeks (measured)
Herbivorous grazing and seasonal mass egg-laying aggregations
records.behavior_model: Triggers: siphon touch -> withdrawal, weakening with repetition; tail shock -> global sensitisation of withdrawal for days; food algae chemistry -> feeding. Needs: red/green algae, clean seawater, conspecifics for breeding aggregations. Goals: graze, avoid harm, breed in season. State changes: sensitised state after shock is a whole-animal mode shift — touchier, darker ink readiness.
records.relationships: Phylum Mollusca, class Gastropoda — kin to Lymnaea in this batch (the other gastropod learning model; the Atlas pairs them deliberately) and distant kin to the cephalopods (Sepia, Nautilus, Doryteuthis).
records.memory_model: Remembers: sensitisation for days (single shock) to weeks (repeated training); habituation for days-weeks; conditioned pairings across days — all published durations. Forgets: memories fade without retraining on the same timescales. Misreads: sensitisation generalises — after a shock, even harmless touches provoke strong withdrawal; the slug over-protects, mechanistically understandably.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Neuron count '~20,000' is the standard textbook figure. CREB/gene-expression account is the consensus molecular story (Kandel); fine details of long-term storage continue to be researched (including debated synaptic-vs-nuclear storage contributions) — consensus core claimed, frontier flagged.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: the reference learning synapse — implement habituation/sensitisation/conditioning parameters directly from the Aplysia literature as BrainKit's plasticity defaults for simple brains.

source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: Air-breathing freshwater snail (~5 cm shell) that surfaces to open a pneumostome. Its aerial-respiration behaviour is operantly conditionable: snails learn to keep the pneumostome closed under hypoxic training, with memory lasting days-weeks and modulated by stress, predator scent and crowding. Aerial respiration circuit (including the neuron RPeD1) is identified. Taste-aversion learning to food chemicals is also documented.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — learning paradigms and the RPeD1 circuit are published (strong anchors); the assembled cognitive profile is the Atlas's, hence the grade stays INFERRED beside Aplysia's MEASURED.
brain_profile.architecture: Ring of ganglia around the oesophagus; the central pattern generator for aerial respiration is a named three-neuron circuit gated by RPeD1, which is also required for memory formation in the conditioning paradigm — a single identified neuron where learning and behaviour meet. Chemoreception dominates its world (food, predators, kin).

regions.name: RPeD1 / respiratory CPG
regions.role: Aerial breathing rhythm and its operant conditioning — memory's gatekeeper neuron

regions.name: Cerebral ganglia
regions.role: Chemosensory learning — food and predator cues

regions.name: Whole-body withdrawal system
regions.role: Predator-scent defensive state

cognition_model.summary: A snail that learns when to hold its breath: it weighs oxygen need against predator risk, remembers its training for weeks, and forgets faster when stressed or crowded — memory ecology studied in a single pond animal.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A cautious, home-water learner: surface carefully, breathe, remember what the water smelled like when it was dangerous, and adjust. Routine and vigilance in a shell.

records.behavior_model: Triggers: hypoxia -> surfacing attempt (suppressed if trained); crayfish/fish scent -> withdrawal and reduced breathing. Needs: oxygenated surface access, calcium for shell, vegetation food. Goals: breathe without being eaten; feed; lay eggs. State changes: predator exposure installs a days-long cautious mode that also rewrites memory persistence.
records.relationships: Class Gastropoda — the deliberate pair to Aplysia (freshwater vs marine gastropod learning models). Ponds across the Northern Hemisphere; a food-web staple for fish and crayfish, hence its educated caution.
records.memory_model: Remembers: respiratory training for days to weeks (single vs spaced training changes duration, as in Aplysia); food aversions across days. Forgets: faster under stress — forgetting itself is studied in this animal. Misreads: predator scent without predators keeps it hiding and under-breathing — a cost of caution.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Memory durations are paradigm- and strain-dependent (laboratory-bred lines differ from wild-caught); figures here are ranges from the Lukowiak-group literature, not constants. RPeD1's necessity is established for the specific conditioning paradigm, not for all snail memory.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: gastropod learning module with an ecology dial — memory persistence as a function of stress/crowding state; RPeD1-style single gating node for behaviour-memory coupling.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)

records.attributes: Large, furry social bee with a brain of roughly a million-plus neurons (order-of-magnitude hymenopteran scale; species estimates vary). Workers learn flower colours/odours rapidly, copy techniques from demonstrators — pulling strings and rolling balls to reach reward in experiments, with the behaviour spreading through the colony socially (2016-2017, published in Science / PLOS Biology). Colonies are annual, founded by a single queen, a few hundred workers at peak.

brain_profile.grade_note: MEASURED — the string-pulling and ball-rolling social-learning results, plus flower-learning and trade-off studies, are published experimental findings on this species.
brain_profile.architecture: Hymenopteran plan like the pilot honeybee — mushroom bodies for associative learning, optic lobes, antennal lobes — in a larger, hardier bee. Social learning is the headline: an observer bee acquires a novel technique by watching a trained demonstrator, a capacity once assumed beyond insects.

cognition_model.summary: The innovator bee: individuals invent or copy solutions to problems no bee evolved for (rolling a ball to a goal for sugar), and the trick spreads culturally through the colony. Published, replicated, and still startling.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A sociable enthusiast-learner: quick to try, quick to copy a neighbour's bright idea, tireless between flowers — curiosity with a colony behind it.

skills: Social learning of novel techniques (string-pulling, ball-rolling — published)

records.behavior_model: Triggers: novel object near reward -> manipulation trials; demonstrator success -> copying attempts. Needs: continuous flower forage through the season, nest site, queen survival. Goals: colony stores and new queens/drones by autumn. State changes: colony phase (founding -> growth -> reproduction) rewires every worker's priorities.
records.relationships: Family Apidae — kin to the pilot Apis mellifera (same family, different genus and colony design: annual and small vs perennial and huge). The Atlas keeps them as separate records with the kinship stated, per the task's skip-bees instruction for the pilot species only.
records.memory_model: Remembers: flower rewards and learned techniques for days-weeks; techniques persist and spread after the inventor is gone (colony culture in the studies' framing). Forgets: unrewarded flower types fade. Misreads: artificial flowers exploit its rules — it generalises boldly, sometimes wrongly, then corrects.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Ball-rolling bees were trained with model demonstrators in the key study (live demonstrators also worked); 'culture' language is the papers' own cautious framing ('social learning / behavioural spread'), kept here. Neuron count is an order-of-magnitude hymenopteran figure, not a Bombus census.

records.attributes: Queens found annual colonies in spring, in hollows and wall voids, reaching a few hundred workers in paper nests. Workers hunt live insects at dusk and even at lights at night — unusual among wasps. Learning follows the wasp pattern (place, prey and nest-site learning documented across vespids); hornet-specific cognition studies are thinner than bee/ant work, and the grade reflects that.

brain_profile.architecture: Standard hymenopteran brain: mushroom bodies for learning (nest location, hunting grounds), strong optic lobes for crepuscular/nocturnal hunting — Vespa eyes are built for low light. Colony cognition is queen-founded and seasonal, closer to Bombus's annual design than to Apis's perennial one.

cognition_model.summary: The night-shift wasp: a big, surprisingly measured predator that hunts moths at lamps, defends its paper city hard, and otherwise wants to be left alone. Reputation exceeds aggression in the documented record.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: A formidable but orderly colony citizen-soldier: hunt by the shift, defend the nest without hesitation, keep the paper city running until autumn ends it.

records.behavior_model: Triggers: nest disturbance -> mass defence; dusk -> hunting flights; lamp light -> moth hunting. Needs: nest cavity, insect prey, carbohydrates (sap/fruit). records.relationships: Family Vespidae. Atlas relations: predator of the batch's bees (Bombus) and a fellow hymenopteran of Atta and the pilot Apis — one order, four social designs, all recorded separately.
records.memory_model: Remembers: nest location and profitable hunting features (family-typical, inferred for this species). Despite folklore, it is not uniquely radiation-proof — hardier than humans, less so than some insects.

records.memory_model: Remembers: (kin evidence) shelter-avoidance and maze routes for days. Forgets: untested — honest blank for this species. Misreads: baited pots exploit exactly its food-chemistry approach rules — a fishery built on its heuristics.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Species vs kin split is the whole honesty of this record: Cancer pagurus cognition studies are sparse; Carcinus maenas carries the famous learning results. The 2021 LSE sentience review and subsequent UK legal recognition covered decapods as an order — reported as policy fact, not as proof about this species' experience.

records.origin: Real species; a marine placozoan — possibly the simplest free-living animal body plan known: a flat disc of a few thousand cells, no neurons, no gut, no muscles, no symmetry axis. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)

source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: Two epithelial layers with fibre cells between, ciliated below for gliding, a few millimetres across. It feeds by settling on algae and digesting externally beneath its body. Cells coordinate via peptide signals — it possesses much of the molecular toolkit that other animals built nervous systems from, deployed without a single neuron. Behaviour includes directed gliding, pausing on food, and body-shape changes coordinated across the disc.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — cell biology and behaviour documented; there is no cognition, and this record is the Atlas's proof that coordination predates neurons.
brain_profile.architecture: No nervous system, no synapses — but peptidergic secretory cells act as a slow broadcast network, the evolutionary raw material of neural signalling. Gliding coordination emerges from ciliary beating coupled through the epithelium: a consensus of cells with no conductor, simpler even than the sponge's arrangement in cell-type terms (though the sponge record holds the size record).

records.origin: Real species; soil social amoeba — free-living single cells that, when starved, aggregate by the hundred-thousand into a migrating slug and then a fruiting body, ~20% of cells dying to build the stalk. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)
Established Dictyostelium literature (cAMP relay aggregation, slug phototaxis/thermotaxis, altruistic stalk differentiation)
source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: Amoebae hunt bacteria alone until food runs out; then cells pulse cAMP, neighbours relay the signal, and streams converge into a multicellular slug that migrates toward light and heat gradients, chooses where to fruit, and sacrifices its stalk cells so spores can disperse. Chimeras can cheat (under-contribute to stalk) — documented social conflict in a microbe. Some clones 'farm' bacteria, carrying food stocks into the fruiting body (published 2011).

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — aggregation signalling and slug behaviour are MEASURED-grade cell biology; framing the slug as a cognitive agent is the Atlas's colony-style modelling choice, stated openly (as with the termite colony record).
brain_profile.architecture: No neurons at any stage. Coordination is a relay: cAMP pulses propagate cell-to-cell, each cell both receiver and repeater — a chemical internet. The slug integrates light/heat/ammonia gradients across thousands of cells and 'decides' migration vs fruiting as a population-level computation.

regions.name: cAMP relay network
regions.role: Aggregation signalling — the social call to assemble

regions.name: Slug tip organiser region
regions.role: Migration steering by light/heat gradients

regions.name: Differentiation programme (stalk/spore)
regions.role: Altruistic division of labour — 20% die as stalk

cognition_model.summary: Part-time multicellularity: alone when fed, a society when starving — with signalling, migration, altruism, cheating and even bacterial farming, all without a neuron or a permanent body. The Atlas's social-minimum record.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: Pinned as a design metaphor (see Confidence): the ultimate community organiser — when crisis comes it literally calls the neighbourhood together, builds the structure, and gives up its own cells for the group's future.

records.behavior_model: Triggers: starvation -> cAMP pulsing and aggregation; light/heat gradients -> slug migration direction; favourable site -> fruiting switch. Needs: soil bacteria, moisture, a surface to fruit on. Goals: none attributable individually; population-level outcomes are dispersal and survival. State changes: solitary <-> social is the master switch — the same genome, two lifestyles.
records.relationships: Supergroup Amoebozoa — the other slime mould in this batch, and Physarum's perfect foil: Physarum is one giant cell pretending to be many; Dictyostelium is many cells pretending to be one. The Atlas maps them adjacent by design philosophy, not by close taxonomy.
records.memory_model: Remembers: no neural memory. Slug migration integrates current gradients only; spore dormancy is persistence, not memory. 'Farming' clones carry bacteria as cargo — a heritable behaviour, not a learned one, recorded precisely.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Cheating/farming findings come from specific study systems (Nature 2011 for farming) — real but clone-dependent, not species universals. An MBTI read on an amoeba collective is a design metaphor at full stretch, labelled as such.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: two-mode agent — solitary foragers that, on starvation signal, merge into one slug-agent with gradient steering, then split into spore records. The Atlas's merge/split test case.

records.origin: Real species; a trumpet-shaped single cell up to ~1-2 mm — among the largest single cells — famous since Jennings (1906) for its escalating repertoire of avoidance behaviours. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)
Jennings 1906 (public domain) behaviour hierarchy observations
Modern Stentor literature (regeneration, 2022 contractile-response / learning-discussion papers — Marshall lab tradition)
source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: One cell with a macronucleus like a string of beads, cortical rows of cilia, and a contractile body. Jennings described a hierarchy when irritated (e.g. by carmine particles): bend away, reverse cilia, contract, detach and swim off — escalating responses as if choosing among options, in a single cell. It regenerates from fragments (any piece with macronuclear material can rebuild), and recent work revisits its learning with modern rigour.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — the behavioural hierarchy is documented observation (1906, repeatedly confirmed as behaviour); interpreting it as decision-making or learning remains debated, and modern replication-grade learning claims are still being tested. Grade reflects that live status.
brain_profile.architecture: No neurons — the cell cortex is the computer: mechanosensitive channels trigger contraction (myonemes), ciliary reversal is calcium-driven, and response thresholds shift with recent history in ways Jennings read as experience-dependence. Whether that shift is true associative learning or response dynamics is the open question this record preserves.

regions.name: Cortical mechanosensation / contraction system
regions.role: Whole-cell startle contraction in milliseconds

regions.name: Ciliary control system
regions.role: Feeding current vs reversal — the first two rungs of Jennings' ladder

regions.name: Behavioural escalation programme
regions.role: Bend -> reverse -> contract -> leave: ordered fallback responses

cognition_model.summary: A single cell with a repertoire and an order of operations: it tries the cheap defence first and escalates only as the insult persists. Jennings thought it showed the germ of behaviour itself; a century later, science is still carefully checking — and the record keeps both the observation and the checking.

personality.mbti_label: Lore-based interpretive read (fan interpretation) — a behaviour-design lens, not a measurement. Basis here: documented behaviour.
personality.justification: Pinned as a design metaphor (see Confidence): a self-sufficient loner with clear boundaries — tolerate, deflect, flinch, and if it keeps happening, leave and rebuild elsewhere.

records.behavior_model: Triggers: particulate irritation/mechanical disturbance -> escalation ladder. Needs: bacterial food, a substrate to perch on, pondwater chemistry. Goals: none attributable — feeding and integrity as cellular programmes. State changes: attached feeding form vs free-swimming migrant form; contracted vs extended states in milliseconds.
records.relationships: Phylum Ciliophora — kin to Paramecium in this batch (both ciliates: Stentor the giant escalator, Paramecium the swimmer). Historically kin to the birth of behaviour studies: Jennings' 1906 book is a founding text.
records.memory_model: Remembers: response thresholds appear history-dependent (Jennings); rigorous modern verdicts on learning in Stentor are pending/mixed — the record claims the hierarchy, not the learning. Forgets: contraction state resets in seconds. Misreads: inert particles trigger the full ladder — over-inclusion is the design.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: Jennings' interpretations were long dismissed as anthropomorphism, then partly rehabilitated as accurate behaviour description — the dispute arc is part of the record. Any 'Stentor learns' headline should be read against this record's caution. MBTI = design metaphor, labelled.

records.origin: Real species; the slipper-shaped ciliate of every school microscope, ~0.2 mm, swimming by thousands of cilia through pond water. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)
Established ciliate physiology (calcium-based avoiding reaction, membrane excitability — Eckert/Naitoh tradition)
source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: Its avoiding reaction is membrane biophysics: bump at the front -> calcium influx -> cilia reverse -> the cell backs up, turns, and tries a new heading; touch at the rear does the opposite. This excitable membrane — action-potential-like, ion-channel-based — is a functional ancestor of neuronal excitability. Older claims of paramecium learning (e.g. tube-escape training) have a chequered replication history and are not carried as fact.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — excitability and the avoiding reaction are MEASURED physiology; no learning is claimed. The record's value is the membrane itself: excitability before neurons.
brain_profile.architecture: No neurons, one membrane: voltage-gated calcium channels in the cilia turn touch into reversal. Chemosensory inputs bias turning rates (accumulation in good water, dispersal from bad — klinokinesis-like behaviour). The whole sensorimotor loop is a handful of ion channels — E. coli's logic rebuilt in a eukaryote with electricity.

regions.name: Ciliary calcium excitability
regions.role: The avoiding reaction — touch-to-reversal in one membrane event

regions.name: Chemosensory turning bias
regions.role: Accumulation in favourable chemical zones

regions.name: Oral groove / feeding system
regions.role: Bacterial feeding currents and vacuole cycling

cognition_model.summary: The excitable cell: it cannot learn (so far as rigorous evidence shows), but its membrane already speaks the neuron's language — voltage, calcium, all-or-nothing reversal. Included as the eukaryote floor beside E. coli, with a famous history of learning claims the evidence did not sustain.

personality.justification: Pinned as a design metaphor (see Confidence): pure responsive motion — bump, back, turn, go; a life of immediate feedback with no residue.

records.behavior_model: Triggers: frontal mechanical contact -> reversal; favourable chemistry -> reduced turning (stays); starvation/stress -> conjugation readiness. Needs: bacterial food, pond water, oxygen. Goals: none attributable. State changes: dividing vs conjugating life modes; fed vacuole cycling pace.
records.relationships: Phylum Ciliophora — pair with Stentor (same phylum: the honest contrast is Stentor's rich repertoire vs Paramecium's single elegant reflex). Ecological staple: food for Hydra and larval animals in this batch's freshwater web.
records.memory_model: Remembers: nothing beyond membrane/channel states lasting seconds. Historical training claims (Gelber's mid-century work and successors) failed to hold up under scrutiny — recorded here as a cautionary example the Atlas values, not as memory.
records.confidence_and_conflicts: This record deliberately models restraint: a beloved textbook animal where the honest answer on learning is 'not demonstrated'. MBTI = design metaphor, labelled.
records.game_implementation: BrainKit: reflex-only agent — one excitable-membrane rule set; used in the Atlas as the negative control for learning claims (if a design shows 'learning' here, check the design, not the cell).

records.origin: Real species; a filter-feeding sea squirt whose tadpole larva swims with a chordate body plan — notochord, dorsal nerve cord, and a small cerebral vesicle with an eye and a gravity sensor — then settles, resorbs its tail and much of that larval nervous system, and lives sessile. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)
Established Ciona developmental neurobiology (larval connectome studies — Ryan & Meinertzhagen tradition; ~177-neuron larval CNS)
source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: The larva is a miniature chordate: ~177 central neurons (published connectome work), a pigment-cup eye (ocellus) and a statocyst-like otolith for orientation. At metamorphosis it digests its own tail and reduces the cerebral vesicle to a small adult ganglion — the famous (and loosely worded) 'eats its own brain' story; precisely: it resorbs most of the larval CNS because a sessile filter-feeder needs far less of it. Adults retain a cerebral ganglion coordinating siphon and feeding responses.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — larval connectomics are published (MEASURED anchor); adult cognition is minimal and unstudied beyond reflexes, and the record says so.
brain_profile.architecture: Two nervous systems in one life: a larval CNS built for a one-day swimming dispersal (find light, gravity, then a surface), and an adult ganglion built for plumbing (siphon control, water flow, gamete release). Metamorphosis is a controlled demolition between the two designs — the Atlas's clearest record that brains are built for a life-stage, not for life.

regions.name: Larval cerebral vesicle (~177-neuron CNS)
regions.role: Swimming orientation — ocellus light sense + otolith gravity sense

regions.name: Adult cerebral ganglion
regions.role: Siphon reflexes, feeding-current coordination

regions.name: Siphon sensory systems
regions.role: Touch/chemistry-triggered closure — the adult's main behaviour

cognition_model.summary: The chordate that trades its brain for a house: it swims as a tiny tadpole with our own body plan, picks a rock, and remodels itself into a filter. Not degeneration — budgeting. The Atlas keeps the precise version against the pub-quiz version.

personality.justification: Pinned as a design metaphor (see Confidence): explore young, choose once, settle forever — a life in two acts, wanderer then fixture, each with exactly the nervous system it needs.

skills: Larval swimming with eye + gravity orientation
Adult siphon filter-feeding and reflex closure
records.behavior_model: Triggers: larval light/gravity cues + surface contact -> settlement and metamorphosis; adult siphon touch -> instant closure. Needs: hard marine substrate, plankton flow, conspecifics for spawning synchrony. Goals: larva — a site; adult — flow. State changes: metamorphosis is the state change of the Atlas — nervous system, body plan and lifestyle rebuilt in hours.
records.relationships: Phylum Chordata, subphylum Tunicata — our own phylum's early branch: Ciona is closer kin to the reader than to every other record in this batch, a map fact the Atlas should make startling and visible.
records.memory_model: Remembers: nothing studied neurally beyond larval response biases. Settlement 'choice' integrates larval sensory history over minutes-hours. Misreads: ship hulls and harbour walls are accepted as rock — the species is a successful invader partly by undiscriminating settlement.

Larval neuron count ~177 is from connectome papers on Ciona (species-complex taxonomy C. intestinalis / C. robusta has shifted — noted). MBTI = design metaphor, labelled.

records.origin: Real species; a lobate comb jelly of Atlantic American coasts (and a damaging invader in European seas), propelled by eight iridescent comb rows. Ctenophores may have evolved neurons independently of all other animals. REAL shelf.

sources: Wikidata (CC0)
Established ctenophore neurobiology (Moroz and colleagues — independent-origin-of-neurons hypothesis; Mnemiopsis genome, Ryan et al. 2013)
source_and_license.license: Atlas text original; underlying facts from CC0/CC-BY/public-domain sources and published literature cited per record. No fan-wiki text copied.

records.attributes: A gelatinous predator of zooplankton and fish larvae with a nerve net, an apical sensory organ (statocyst) coordinating the comb rows, and a genome that lacks many canonical bilaterian neurotransmitter pathways — evidence behind the published hypothesis that ctenophore neurons evolved independently (a second invention of the neuron). It is bioluminescent, hermaphroditic, and regenerates; invasive populations reshaped the Black Sea food web in the 1980s-90s.

brain_profile.grade_note: INFERRED — genome and neurochemistry are published; the independent-origin hypothesis is influential but debated (flagged), and behaviour-level cognition in Mnemiopsis is little studied.
brain_profile.architecture: Nerve net plus apical organ: comb-row beating is coordinated for steering and escape responses; feeding lobes and auricles funnel prey to the mouth. Chemically it runs a partly different neurotransmitter toolkit (glutamate prominent; several familiar systems absent) — alien wiring solving familiar problems.

regions.role: Balance and comb-row coordination — the steering centre

regions.name: Subepithelial nerve net
regions.role: Whole-body responses, escape and feeding coordination

cognition_model.summary: Possibly evolution's second draft of a neuron: a comb jelly whose nervous system may share no ancestor with ours, built from a different chemical kit. As an animal it is a drifting, glowing plankton-trap — and as an invader, an ecosystem-scale event.
